column1: # The secp256k1 cliff, measured 2026-08-24 on an M4 Max, one job at a time.
# secp256k1's Secp256k1DoubleAssign chip is 167,376 and 251,064 constraint nodes,
# far over the zerocheck node bound, so it never gets a GPU kernel.
# Between n=1000 and n=1500 the Metal arm falls off a cliff while the CPU arm
# does not move and the shard count does not change. This is a defect in the
# Metal path, not a cost of the workload: at n=1500 the CPU arm proves in 7.79 s
# and the Metal arm does not finish in 900.
# SUPERSEDED 2026-08-26: this is not a performance cliff. The Metal arm does
# not finish because it produces a shard proof that does not verify -- the GKR
# round lent overlapping pages -- and SP1 retries it until the budget is gone.
# Fixed; secp256k1 now verifies at every size from 1000 to 4000 at 3.47x-3.59x
# with no discontinuity. See results/gkr-overlapping-lends.md.
# An earlier reading of this cliff was contaminated -- the diagnostic ran
# alongside a stuck 21-minute process -- and was re-measured cleanly.
